'''Jan Saxl''' (5 June 1948 – 2 May 2020) was a Czech-British [[mathematician]], and a professor at the [[University of Cambridge]].  He was known for his work in [[Group theory#Finite group theory|finite group theory]], particularly on consequences of the [[classification of finite simple groups]].

==Education and career==
Saxl was born in [[Brno]], in what was at the time [[Czechoslovakia]].  He came to the [[United Kingdom]] in 1968, during the [[Prague Spring]].<ref name="cambridgeobit">{{cite web|url=https://www.cai.cam.ac.uk/news/professor-jan-saxl|title=Professor Jan Saxl (obituary)|work=Gonville & Caius|publisher=[[University of Cambridge]]|date=5 May 2020|access-date=9 May 2020|archive-date=17 May 2020|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200517214405/https://www.cai.cam.ac.uk/news/professor-jan-saxl|url-status=live}}</ref>  
After undergraduate studies at the [[University of Bristol]],<ref name="cambridgeobit"/> he completed his DPhil in 1973 at the [[University of Oxford]] under the direction of [[Peter M. Neumann]], with the title of ''Multiply Transitive Permutation Groups''.<ref name="mgp">{{MathGenealogy|id=46094}}</ref>

Saxl held postdoctoral positions at Oxford and the [[University of Illinois at Chicago]], and a lecturer position at the [[University of Glasgow]].  He moved to the University of Cambridge in 1976, and spent the rest of his career there.<ref name="cambridgeobit"/><ref name="lmsobit" />  He was elected as a fellow of [[Gonville and Caius College]] in 1986,<ref name="cambridgeobit"/> and he retired in 2015.<ref name="lmsobit">{{cite web|url=https://www.lms.ac.uk/news-entry/05052020-1505/professor-jan-saxl-leading-figure-algebra|title=Professor Jan Saxl: A leading figure in algebra|publisher=[[London Mathematical Society]]|last=Johnson|first=John|date=5 May 2020|access-date=9 May 2020|archive-date=27 January 2021|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210127173645/https://www.lms.ac.uk/news-entry/05052020-1505/professor-jan-saxl-leading-figure-algebra|url-status=live}}</ref>

<!-- In the following, note that the MR link in each paper leads to a secondary overview of the paper, at least from a university IP -->
Saxl published around 100 papers, and according to MathSciNet, these have been cited over 1900 times.<ref name="mathscinet">{{cite web|url=https://mathscinet.ams.org/mathscinet/search/author.html?mrauthid=155270 |title=Jan Saxl author profile|website=[[MathSciNet]]|publisher=American Mathematical Society|url-access=subscription}}</ref>  He is noted for his work in finite group theory, particularly on [[permutation group]]s, and often coauthored with [[Robert Guralnick]], [[Martin Liebeck]], and [[Cheryl Praeger]].  Some notable and highly-cited<ref name="mathscinet" /> examples of this work are as follows.  Liebeck, Saxl and Praeger gave a relatively simple and self-contained [[mathematical proof|proof]] of the [[O'Nan–Scott theorem]].<ref>{{cite journal | last1=Liebeck | first1=Martin W. | last2=Praeger | first2=Cheryl E. | last3=Saxl | first3=Jan | title=On the O'Nan-Scott theorem for finite primitive permutation groups | journal=Journal of the Australian Mathematical Society, Series A | publisher=Cambridge University Press (CUP) | volume=44 | issue=3 | year=1988 | issn=0263-6115 | doi=10.1017/s144678870003216x| mr=0929529 | pages=389–396| doi-access=free }}</ref>  It had long been known that every [[maximal subgroup]] of a [[symmetric group]] or [[alternating group]] was intransitive, imprimitive, or primitive, and the same authors in 1988 gave a partial description of which primitive subgroups could occur.<ref>{{cite journal | last1=Liebeck | first1=Martin W | last2=Praeger | first2=Cheryl E | last3=Saxl | first3=Jan | title=A classification of the maximal subgroups of the finite alternating and symmetric groups | journal=Journal of Algebra | publisher=Elsevier BV | volume=111 | issue=2 | year=1987 | issn=0021-8693 | doi=10.1016/0021-8693(87)90223-7 |mr=0916173 | pages=365–383| doi-access=free }}</ref><ref>{{cite book | last=Wilson | first=Robert | title=The finite simple groups | publisher=Springer | publication-place=London New York | year=2009 | isbn=978-1-84800-988-2 | oclc=535009535 | page=4}}</ref>

==Personal life==
Saxl was married to Cambridge mathematician [[Ruth Margaret Williams|Ruth M. Williams]] and they had one daughter, Miriam.<ref name="cambridgeobit" />

==Death==
Saxl died on 2 May 2020, after a long period of poor health.<ref name="cambridgeobit"/>

==Awards and honors==
A three-day conference in the joint honor of Saxl and Martin Liebeck was held at the University of Cambridge in July 2015.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.lms.ac.uk/sites/lms.ac.uk/files/files/May%202015.pdf|title=Simple Groups, Representations and Related Topics (conference announcement)|work=Newsletter|publisher=[[London Mathematical Society]]|issue=447|year=2015|access-date=9 May 2020|archive-date=24 January 2021|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210124064714/https://www.lms.ac.uk/sites/lms.ac.uk/files/files/May%202015.pdf|url-status=live}}</ref>
